title: Who may have a prescription drug dispensed in a noncomplying (conventional) package
subtopic: Poison prevention packaging of prescription drugs
rule_summary: Under 15 U.S.C. 1473(b), in the case of a household substance which is subject to a special packaging standard and which is dispensed pursuant to an order of a physician, dentist, or other licensed medical practitioner authorized to prescribe, such substance may be dispensed in noncomplying packages only when directed in such order or when requested by the purchaser. Separately, 15 U.S.C. 1473(a) permits a manufacturer or packer, to make a household substance subject to a standard readily available to elderly or handicapped persons unable to use it in complying packages, to package the substance in noncomplying packaging of a single size if it also supplies the substance in complying packages and the noncomplying packages bear conspicuous labeling stating 'This package for households without young children'.
exam_relevance: Tests the two statutory routes to a conventional container for a prescription drug, the prescriber's direction in the order and the purchaser's request, and keeps them apart from the manufacturer's single-size allowance in 15 U.S.C. 1473(a).

authority.name: Poison Prevention Packaging Act of 1970: conventional packages

common_confusions: Treating the pharmacist's own judgment that a patient has no young children as a basis for a conventional container.
Assuming a prescriber's direction for one prescription extends to the patient's other prescriptions.
verification_notes: 15 U.S.C. 1473 read on uscode.house.gov (chapter 39A, current edition) during the authoring session of 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-17.
